- If sentiment is consistently negative or low (e.g., < 0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment turns positive sharply (e.g., > 0.7) after a dip, model often underreacts; increase forecast slightly (e.g., +1–2%) to capture momentum.  
- When model shows steady upward trend with no volatility, true outcome often exhibits mean reversion or sharp downward correction — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.  
- After a model forecast spike (e.g., > +5% from prior), true outcome often corrects downward — apply “overshoot correction” by subtracting 2–5% from forecast peak.  
- If sentiment history shows multiple consecutive low values (e.g., 3+ days < 0.4), model tends to underestimate — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for suppressed sentiment.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates > 5% from model in first 5–7 days, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day mean, not 30-day trend.  
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model often overestimates — reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect sentiment mismatch.
